Thank you for the opportunity to share my thoughts.

I found Q3.4 challenging because using online activity data feels invasive, but I also see its potential benefits. The questions about sensitive data were tough too—I worried about privacy but also understood the need for fairness.

The most important question for me was Q5.2. Ensuring that all student groups are equally supported is crucial. If the model works better for some and worse for others, it risks deepening existing inequalities.

I noticed a strong consensus on avoiding very low explainability (Q4.1), which aligns with my view. However, I wonder if moderate or even high explainability could still miss important nuances in student experiences.

An opt-out mechanism might help balance privacy concerns with the need for support. Thank you.

I found Q3.4 and questions about sensitive data particularly challenging because they force us to balance privacy with the need for support. As someone who previously dropped out of a programme, I understand how crucial early intervention can be. However, using online activity data feels too intrusive, as it might make students feel constantly monitored.

For me, Q5.2 was also very important. Ensuring equal recall across all student groups is essential to prevent further marginalization of already disadvantaged students.

I noticed that everyone avoided very low explainability (Q4.1), which aligns with my view. Moderate explainability seems like a reasonable compromise, as it provides some insight without being overly complex.

An opt-out mechanism could help address concerns about privacy and surveillance while still ensuring that those who need support receive it. Thank you.
